req.title: Task update persists
req.statement: The system shall persist PUT changes so subsequent GET requests reflect the update.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that PUT /tasks/{task_id} persists changes so a subsequent GET reflects the update. I design: (1) a positive EP/STC test that creates a task, PUTs all mutable fields, then GETs and asserts exact values; (2) a negative NEG test that PUTs to a non-existent task_id and asserts exactly HTTP 404; (3) a BVA boundary test that updates the title to exactly 1 character (min_length boundary) and to 100 characters (max_length boundary), asserting persistence of both; (4) a DT test covering partial updates (only one field at a time) to verify exclude_unset logic; (5) a STC test verifying the completed flag transitions false→true→false and persists each state. All tests use in-process TestClient, create their own data, and assert exact values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_put_persists_all_fields_positive
preconditions: A task is created via POST /tasks/
actions: POST /tasks/ with title='Original', description='Old desc', completed=false
PUT /tasks/{id} with title='Updated', description='New desc', completed=true
expected: PUT response body contains updated title, description, completed=true
GET response body matches PUT response exactly for title, description, completed
trace: R-TASK-022: PUT changes must be reflected in subsequent GET
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_persists_all_fields_positive():
    post_r = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Original", "description": "Old desc", "completed": False})
    assert post_r.status_code == 201
    task_id = post_r.json()["id"]

    put_r = client.put(f"/tasks/{task_id}", json={"title": "Updated", "description": "New desc", "completed": True})
    assert put_r.status_code == 200
    put_body = put_r.json()
    assert put_body["id"] == task_id
    assert put_body["title"] == "Updated"
    assert put_body["description"] == "New desc"
    assert put_body["completed"] is True

    get_r = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert get_r.status_code == 200
    get_body = get_r.json()
    assert get_body["id"] == task_id
    assert get_body["title"] == "Updated"
    assert get_body["description"] == "New desc"
    assert get_body["completed"] is True

tests.name: test_put_title_boundary_min_and_max_length
preconditions: Two tasks are created via POST
actions: PUT first task with title of exactly 1 character (min_length boundary)
GET first task and assert title == 'A'
PUT second task with title of exactly 100 characters (max_length boundary)
GET second task and assert title equals the 100-char string
expected: PUT with 1-char title returns HTTP 200 and persists
PUT with 100-char title returns HTTP 200 and persists
PUT with 0-char title returns HTTP 422 (below min boundary)
PUT with 101-char title returns HTTP 422 (above max boundary)
trace: R-TASK-022: persistence must hold at schema boundary values; BVA ±1 catches off-by-one in field validation
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_title_boundary_min_and_max_length():
    r1 = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task One", "completed": False})
    assert r1.status_code == 201
    id1 = r1.json()["id"]

    r2 = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task Two", "completed": False})
    assert r2.status_code == 201
    id2 = r2.json()["id"]

    min_title = "A"
    put_min = client.put(f"/tasks/{id1}", json={"title": min_title})
    assert put_min.status_code == 200
    assert put_min.json()["title"] == "A"
    get_min = client.get(f"/tasks/{id1}")
    assert get_min.status_code == 200
    assert get_min.json()["title"] == "A"

    max_title = "X" * 100
    put_max = client.put(f"/tasks/{id2}", json={"title": max_title})
    assert put_max.status_code == 200
    assert put_max.json()["title"] == max_title
    get_max = client.get(f"/tasks/{id2}")
    assert get_max.status_code == 200
    assert get_max.json()["title"] == max_title

    put_zero = client.put(f"/tasks/{id1}", json={"title": ""})
    assert put_zero.status_code == 422

    put_over = client.put(f"/tasks/{id2}", json={"title": "Y" * 101})
    assert put_over.status_code == 422

tests.name: test_put_partial_update_preserves_untouched_fields
preconditions: A task is created with title, description, and completed=false
actions: GET /tasks/{id} and verify title and description are unchanged
trace: R-TASK-022: exclude_unset partial update must not overwrite unmentioned fields
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_partial_update_preserves_untouched_fields():
    post_r = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Keep Me", "description": "Keep this too", "completed": False})
    assert post_r.status_code == 201
    task_id = post_r.json()["id"]

    put_r = client.put(f"/tasks/{task_id}", json={"completed": True})
    assert put_r.status_code == 200
    put_body = put_r.json()
    assert put_body["completed"] is True
    assert put_body["title"] == "Keep Me"
    assert put_body["description"] == "Keep this too"

    get_r = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert get_r.status_code == 200
    get_body = get_r.json()
    assert get_body["completed"] is True
    assert get_body["title"] == "Keep Me"
    assert get_body["description"] == "Keep this too"
    assert get_body["id"] == task_id

tests.name: test_put_completed_state_transitions_false_true_false
preconditions: A task is created with completed=false
actions: PUT /tasks/{id} with completed=true; GET and assert completed is True
PUT /tasks/{id} with completed=false; GET and assert completed is False
expected: After first PUT: GET returns completed=true
After second PUT: GET returns completed=false
trace: R-TASK-022: state transitions must persist; catches boolean negation mutations and and->or mutations
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_completed_state_transitions_false_true_false():
    post_r = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "State Task", "completed": False})
    assert post_r.status_code == 201
    task_id = post_r.json()["id"]
    assert post_r.json()["completed"] is False

    put1 = client.put(f"/tasks/{task_id}", json={"completed": True})
    assert put1.status_code == 200
    assert put1.json()["completed"] is True
    get1 = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert get1.status_code == 200
    assert get1.json()["completed"] is True

    put2 = client.put(f"/tasks/{task_id}", json={"completed": False})
    assert put2.status_code == 200
    assert put2.json()["completed"] is False
    get2 = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert get2.status_code == 200
    assert get2.json()["completed"] is False

tests.name: test_put_invalid_payload_returns_422
actions: PUT /tasks/{id} with completed as a non-boolean string value
expected: Response body contains validation error detail
trace: R-TASK-022: HTTP 4xx on client error — malformed payload must not persist
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_invalid_payload_returns_422():
    post_r = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Valid Task", "completed": False})
    assert post_r.status_code == 201
    task_id = post_r.json()["id"]

    put_r = client.put(f"/tasks/{task_id}", json={"completed": "not-a-bool", "title": ""})
    assert put_r.status_code == 422
    body = put_r.json()
    assert "detail" in body

    get_r = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert get_r.status_code == 200
    assert get_r.json()["title"] == "Valid Task"
    assert get_r.json()["completed"] is False
